arxiv-2204-00988.title: Whose Advantage? Measuring Attention Dynamics across YouTube and Twitter on Controversial Topics
arxiv-2204-00988.creator: JooYoung Lee, Siqi Wu, Ali Mert Ertugrul, Yu-Ru Lin, Lexing Xie
arxiv-2204-00988.description: Abstract The ideological asymmetries have been recently observed in contested online spaces, where conservative voices seem to be relatively more pronounced even though liberals are known to have the population advantage on digital platforms. Most prior research, however, focused on either one single platform or one single political topic.

arxiv-2205-07016.title: A note on the class number of certain real cyclotomic fields
arxiv-2205-07016.creator: Om Prakash
arxiv-2205-07016.description: Abstract . We construct an infinite family of real cyclotomic fields with non-trivial class group. This result generalizes the result in [ 1 ] in the sense that our family includes theirs. 2010 Mathematics Subject Classification Primary: 11D09, 11R29 Secondary: 11R11, 11R18 1. Introduction The ring of rational integers \mathbb{Z} has unique factorization of integers into primes.

arxiv-2303-05291.title: Harnessing quantumness of states using discrete Wigner functions under (non)-Markovian quantum channels
arxiv-2303-05291.creator: Jai Lalita, K. G. Paulson, Subhashish Banerjee
arxiv-2303-05291.description: A 2023 arXiv research paper by Jai Lalita, K. G. Paulson, Subhashish Banerjee. The negativity of the discrete Wigner functions (DWFs) is a measure of non-classicality and is often used to quantify the degree of quantum coherence in a system. The study of Wigner negativity and its evolution under different quantum channels can provide insight into the stability and robustness of quantum states under their interaction with the environment, which is essential for developing practical quantum computing systems.

arxiv-2307-07437.title: Leveraging Traceability to Integrate Safety Analysis Artifacts into the Software Development Process
arxiv-2307-07437.creator: Ankit Agrawal, Jane Cleland-Huang
arxiv-2307-07437.description: Abstract Safety-critical system’s failure or malfunction can cause loss of human lives or damage to the physical environment; therefore, continuous safety assessment is crucial for such systems. In many domains this includes the use of Safety assurance cases (SACs) as a structured argument that the system is safe for use.

arxiv-2308-05209.title: Black Holes with Abelian and Non-Abelian Charges and Their Impact on Matter Accretion Flows
arxiv-2308-05209.creator: Gabriel Gómez, Ángel Rincón, Norman Cruz
arxiv-2308-05209.description: Abstract In this paper, we study the black hole spacetime structure of a model consisting of the standard Maxwell theory and a p p -power-Yang-Mills term. This non-linear contribution introduces a non-Abelian charge into the global solution, resulting in a modified structure of the standard Reissner-Nordström black hole.

arxiv-2407-03777.title: Semi- and Fully-Discrete Analysis of Lowest-Order Nonstandard Finite Element Methods for the Biharmonic Wave Problem
arxiv-2407-03777.creator: Neela Nataraj, Ricardo Ruiz-Baier, Aamir Yousuf
arxiv-2407-03777.description: Abstract Abstract: This paper discusses lowest-order nonstandard finite element methods for space discretization and explicit and implicit schemes for time discretization of the biharmonic wave equation with clamped boundary conditions. A modified Ritz projection operator defined on H^{2}_{0}(\Omega) ensures error estimates under appropriate regularity assumptions on the solution.

arxiv-2407-16656.title: Repeated Block Averages: entropic time and mixing profiles
arxiv-2407-16656.creator: Pietro Caputo, Matteo Quattropani, Federico Sau
arxiv-2407-16656.description: Abstract . We consider randomized dynamics over the n n -simplex, where at each step a random set, or block , of coordinates is evenly averaged. When all blocks have size 2, this reduces to the repeated averages studied in [ CDSZ22 ] , a version of the averaging process on a graph [ AL12 ] .

freeman-pembroke-1894.creator: Mary E. Wilkins Freeman
freeman-pembroke-1894.description: Pembroke: A Novel (1894). Mary E. Wilkins Freeman.

pmc-10637836.title: Personalized accelerated physiologic pacing
pmc-10637836.creator: Markus Meyer, Margaret Infeld, Nicole Habel, Daniel Lustgarten
pmc-10637836.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2023). Heart failure with preserved ejection fraction (HFpEF) is increasingly prevalent with a high socioeconomic burden. Pharmacological heart rate lowering was recommended to improve ventricular filling in HFpEF. This article discusses the misperceptions that have resulted in an overprescription of beta-blockers, which in all likelihood have untoward effects on patients with HFpEF, even if they have atrial fibrillation or coronary artery disease as a comorbidity.

pmc-11318136.title: Lipid accumulation product and type 2 diabetes risk: a population-based study
pmc-11318136.creator: Sepehr Sadafi, Ali Azizi, Farid Najafi, Yahya Pasdar
pmc-11318136.description: BackgroundThe Lipid Accumulation Product (LAP) is a measure that indicates excessive fat accumulation in the body. LAP has been the focus of research in epidemiological studies aimed at forecasting chronic and metabolic diseases. This study aimed to evaluate the association between LAP and type 2 diabetes mellitus (T2DM) among adults in western Iran.

pmc-11321125.title: Dysregulation of plasma circulating microRNAs in all-cause and cause-specific cancers: the Rotterdam Study
pmc-11321125.creator: Yu Shuai, Xiaofang Zhang, Birgit D. A. Lavrijssen, M. Arfan Ikram, Rikje Ruiter, Bruno Stricker, Mohsen Ghanbari
pmc-11321125.description: MicroRNAs (miRNAs) are small non-coding RNAs involved in post-transcriptional regulation of gene expression. Mounting evidence underscores the dysregulation of miRNAs to be associated with cancer development and progression by acting as tumour suppressors and oncogenes. However, their potential as biomarkers for early diagnosis of different cancers remains incompletely unraveled.

pmc-11462666.title: Complete genome sequences of two Pantoea stewartii strains ATCC 8199 from maize and PSCN1 from sugarcane
pmc-11462666.creator: Na Chu, Tian-Tian Liu, Hui-Li Zhang, Dong Cui, Mei-Ting Huang, Hua-Ying Fu, Jun-Bo Su, San-Ji Gao
pmc-11462666.description: ObjectivesThe pathogen of Pantoea stewartii (Ps) is the causal agent of bacterial disease in corn and various graminaceous plants. Ps has two subspecies, Pantoea stewartii subsp. stewartia (Pss) and Pantoea stewartii subsp. indologenes (Psi). This study presents two complete genomes of Ps strains including ATCC 8199 isolated from maize and PSCN1 causing bacterial wilt in sugarcane.

pmc-11492618.title: Trends in CT examination utilization in the emergency department during and after the COVID-19 pandemic
pmc-11492618.creator: Felix Kempter, Tobias Heye, Jan Vosshenrich, Benjamin Ceresa, Dominik Jäschke
pmc-11492618.description: BackgroundThe increasing use of CT imaging in emergency departments, despite efforts of reducing low-value imaging, is not fully understood, especially during and after the COVID-19 pandemic. The aim of this study was to investigate the impact of COVID-19 pandemic related measures on trends and volume in CT examinations requested in the emergency department.

pmc-11580720.title: m6A demethylase FTO transcriptionally activated by SP1 improves ischemia reperfusion‐triggered acute kidney injury by activating Ambra1/ULK1 ‐mediated autophagy
pmc-11580720.creator: Yan Chen, Yuanfei Liu, Weiping Tu, Yanxia Chen, Chengyun Xu, Chong Huang
pmc-11580720.description: Ischemia reperfusion (I/R) was considered as one of main causes of acute kidney injury (AKI). However, the exact mechanism remains unclear. Here, this study aimed to investigate the role and mechanism of the m6A demethylase fat mass and obesity‐associated (FTO) protein in I/R‐induced AKI. HK‐2 cells and SD rats were utilized to establish hypoxia/reoxygenation (H/R) or I/R induced AKI models.

pmc-11593489.title: Interferon Regulatory Factors (IRF1, IRF4, IRF5, IRF7 and IRF9) in Sichuan taimen (Hucho bleekeri): Identification and Functional Characterization
pmc-11593489.creator: Yeyu Chen, Huanchao Yang, Xiaoyun Wu, Zhao Liu, Yanling Chen, Qinyao Wei, Jue Lin, Yi Yu, Quanyu Tu, Hua Li, Alexander V Ereskovsky
pmc-11593489.description: Background/Objectives: Interferon regulatory factors (IRFs) are multifunctional transcription factors that play important roles in the transcriptional regulation of interferons and in the immune response to pathogens. Therefore, studying the interferon system in fish is highly relevant in the prevention and treatment of viral diseases.

pmc-11648071.title: Development of a Proteomic Workflow for the Identification of Heparan Sulphate Proteoglycan‐Binding Substrates of ADAM17
pmc-11648071.creator: Matteo Calligaris, Donatella Pia Spanò, Maria Chiara Puccio, Stephan A. Müller, Simone Bonelli, Margot Lo Pinto, Giovanni Zito, Carl P. Blobel, Stefan F. Lichtenthaler, Linda Troeberg, Simone Dario Scilabra
pmc-11648071.description: Ectodomain shedding, which is the proteolytic release of transmembrane proteins from the cell surface, is crucial for cell‐to‐cell communication and other biological processes. The metalloproteinase ADAM17 mediates ectodomain shedding of over 50 transmembrane proteins ranging from cytokines and growth factors, such as TNF and EGFR ligands, to signalling receptors and adhesion molecules.

pmc-12534562.title: Plant growth-promoting bacteria modulate metabolism and nitrogen accumulation to counteract drought damage in cactus pear plants
pmc-12534562.creator: Gonçalves Albino Dauala, Bruno Sousa Figueiredo da Fonseca, Acacyara Batista de Sousa, Stelamaris de Oliveira Paula-Marinho, Pâmalla Graziely Carvalho Morais, Marcos Renan Lima Leite, Rodrigo Fonseca da Silva, Rhaiana Oliveira de Aviz, Maria Helena Ferreira Duarte, Romilda Rodrigues Nascimento, Elai
pmc-12534562.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2025). Searching sustainable management techniques to enhance plant resistance to drought is crucial for agriculture in stressful scenarios. This study aimed to investigate the role of Plant Growth-Promoting Bacteria (PGPB) strains on forage cactus pear performance under drought. Trials were conducted in greenhouse using forage cactus plants in randomized block experimental design, 8 × 2 factorial scheme, consisting of eight inoculation treatments [inoculation with Paenibacillus sp.

pmc-12693883.title: Bio-Assay-Guided Study of Chaenomeles japonica–Cytokine Modulation by Fruit Aqueous Extract In Vitro in Connection with Its Processing with Enzymatic and Microbial Additives
pmc-12693883.creator: Agata J. Olędzka, Aleksandra Sirak, Dariia Hovtvian, Oleh Koshovyi, Monika E. Czerwińska
pmc-12693883.description: Background/Objectives: Phytochemicals from Chaenomeles japonica (CJ) (Thunb.) Lindl. ex Spach, a plant belonging to the Rosaceae family, are recognized for their potential to inhibit enzymes associated with diabetes, obesity, neurodegeneration, and inflammation. However, the influence of constituents from different plant parts on cytokine secretion has not yet been explored or comparatively analyzed.

pmc-13237233.title: High-resolution distribution map of apple orchards in China based on multisource data
pmc-13237233.creator: Wenqiang Xie, Yunkun Song, Xuefeng Cui, Xiaodong Yan, Shuaifeng Song
pmc-13237233.description: China is the world’s leading apple producer and vital to global fruit supply and food security. Apple production depends on yield and planting area, both strongly influenced by climate. Regional climate variations cause differing cultivation suitability, exacerbating production disparities. Although climate models can project impacts on apples, the lack of high-resolution distribution data limits reliable large-scale assessment.

pmc-13327172.title: Genetic Landscape of Hearing Loss in Brazilian Patients Reveals Population‐Specific Variants and Clinical Correlations
pmc-13327172.creator: Stella Diogo‐Cavassana, Danillo Alencar‐Coutinho, Rafaella Abreu‐Oberhuber, Maria Eduarda Paramo‐Neto, Jeanne Oiticica, Ricardo Ferreira Bento, Ana Carla Batissoco, Karina Lezirovitz
pmc-13327172.description: Hearing loss (HL) is the most prevalent sensory disorder globally and a major public health challenge in Brazil, affecting over 1.5 million individuals. While over 150 HL‐associated genes have been identified, the genetic architecture in underrepresented populations remains poorly defined, often limiting diagnostic yield and precision medicine.

pmc-13366900.title: Psychometric properties of the Night Eating Questionnaire (NEQ) in a clinical sample of Turkish adolescents
pmc-13366900.creator: Mehmet Akif Akıncı, Bahadır Turan, Kübra Bayındır, Furkan Can Tuzcu, Esen Yıldırım Demirdöğen, Abdullah Bozkurt
pmc-13366900.description: BackgroundThis study aimed to examine the psychometric properties of the Turkish version of the Night Eating Questionnaire (NEQ) in an adolescent clinical sample.MethodsThe sample consisted of 267 adolescents aged 13–17 years (64.8% girls; mean age = 15.23 ± 1.29 years) recruited from child and adolescent psychiatry outpatient clinics of two university hospitals in Türkiye.

uslaw-usc-t26-s6802.title: 26 U.S.C. § 6802 — Supply and distribution
uslaw-usc-t26-s6802.creator: United States Congress
uslaw-usc-t26-s6802.description: United States Code, Title 26 (Internal Revenue Code); Chapter 69 (General Provisions Relating To Stamps). Current through Public Law 119-134, as published by the Office of the Law Revision Counsel. The Secretary shall furnish, without prepayment, to— (1) Postmaster General The Postmaster General a suitable quantity of adhesive stamps, coupons, tickets, or such other devices as may be prescribed by the Secretary pursuant to section 6302(b) or this chapter, to be distributed.
